questions: When an authorized visible photo's source object is missing, must the failure be storage-unavailable, or may it be not-found?
When an authorized, visible progress photo’s source object is missing, must the response be the explicit storage-unavailable error, or may it be the not-found failure allowed by A14?

Which exact photo failures count as "stored content cannot be delivered", and must missing, oversize, unlisted media, unreadable storage and invalid file references all become the same storage-unavailable error rather than not-found or a distinct size/media/storage error?

judgement.why: P1 already decides that every listed post-authorization photo storage failure becomes BinaryStorageError and remains distinct from PhotoValidationError.

precedent.topic: Failure classification and response mapping for authorized binary delivery
quotes:
`BinaryStorageError` for an unsafe, missing, oversize, unreadable or
unrecognised object.

`BinaryAccessRejected` for a missing record, another project's or an
invisible one, and an unreadable object alike.

`PhotoValidationError` for a missing, another project's or an invisible
photo; `BinaryStorageError` for an unreadable object. Unlike documents, the
accepted service does not fold these into one answer.
precedent.why: State 5 classifies every listed post-authorization storage failure as BinaryStorageError, folds all such document failures into BinaryAccessRejected, and lets the photo BinaryStorageError propagate.

topics.topic: Expense-document missing, oversize, or unlisted-content failure mapping
questions: For an otherwise authorized, client-visible expense document whose source object is absent, is the response the concealed unknown/hidden response or an explicit storage-unavailable/not-found response?

Must every missing, oversize or unlisted expense-document failure use exactly the concealed unknown/hidden response, or may any of them be exposed as a distinct unavailable or content-policy failure under A14?

judgement.why: P1 already decides that missing, oversize, unreadable, unsafe, and unrecognised document storage failures become BinaryStorageError internally and are folded into BinaryAccessRejected for the caller.

topics.topic: Expense-document storage I/O and invalid-reference failure mapping
questions: How must an authorized document read fail for storage I/O errors not classified as missing, oversize or unlisted, such as permission denial, corrupt file_ref resolution, or an interrupted read?

judgement.why: P1 already covers unsafe and unreadable objects, including invalid-reference and storage I/O failures, and decides that document reads fold them into BinaryAccessRejected.
